events.continuity_hook: Moves the Denver conference plan from comparison into reservations after the agenda change and room opening.
events.interaction_goal: Choose the flight set and hotel, note the room type, request window seats, plan breakfast and dinners, decide airport ground transport, and capture cancellation and reimbursement details.
events.scenario_brief: Tessa is ready to reserve the Denver conference trip. The Sunday afternoon Salt Lake City to Denver nonstop still gives a calm check-in before the Monday late-morning roundtable, and a Wednesday midafternoon return fits after the closing lunch without a long airport wait. The official downtown hotel block has one room left with a firmer cancellation date, no included breakfast, and costly parking, while the nearby breakfast-included hotel is easier for meals but farther from the meeting rooms. Since she can avoid a rental car, the main unresolved choice is venue proximity versus easier breakfast.

events.continuity_hook: Handles the final Denver timing details after bookings are set.
events.interaction_goal: Set the Sunday airport-to-hotel plan, Monday morning timeline, quick breakfast options, badge pickup timing, Wednesday bag storage, and departure buffer for the return flight.
events.scenario_brief: Four days before departure, the conference app adds Sunday evening badge pickup and says Monday roundtable seating starts earlier than planned. Her flights and downtown block hotel are booked, but the hotel breakfast gap and airport-transfer plan still need tightening. The Denver airport train has planned evening maintenance, so she needs a rideshare fallback and a Wednesday luggage plan before the closing lunch and midafternoon flight.

events.continuity_hook: Begins the first fall recruitment planning episode after the Denver conference is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Compare routing options, estimate drive times, shortlist Portland-area, mid-valley, and Seattle-area hotels, note breakfast and restaurant access, and identify flight and car holds worth placing.
events.scenario_brief: About seven weeks before late-August travel, Tessa starts planning a Pacific Northwest recruitment loop. The draft schedule has Monday high-school visits in Portland, a Tuesday evening college fair in Beaverton, a Wednesday morning counselor breakfast in Eugene, a Thursday afternoon Tacoma visit, and a Thursday evening Seattle fair. Salt Lake City has nonstop options into Portland and home from Seattle, but round-tripping through Portland is cheaper and adds backtracking. The unresolved pieces are open-jaw versus round-trip routing, rental car versus rail for the Oregon-to-Washington stretch, and hotel bases that keep early mornings and evening meals manageable.

events.continuity_hook: Refines the fall loop after event times, parking notes, and car pricing change.
events.interaction_goal: Rebuild the hotel sequence, compare the Friday return flights, decide rental-car timing, flag breakfast gaps, map dinner options after the fair, and list the holds that need action soon.
events.scenario_brief: The Pacific Northwest schedule firms up: the Beaverton fair posts an 8:30 p.m. end time, the Eugene breakfast moves to 7:45 a.m., and the Seattle venue warns that load-in parking will be limited. The Sunday afternoon Portland flight remains workable, but the Friday Seattle return choices are a Delta midafternoon nonstop or a cheaper early flight with more morning pressure. One-way car rates now vary sharply by pickup and return hour. Tessa needs to decide whether to split Tuesday night in Salem or Albany instead of pushing all the way to Eugene, keep the car for the full loop, and choose a Seattle-area base that will not complicate the Friday airport return.

events.continuity_hook: Moves the Pacific Northwest route, car, and hotel plan into reservations.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the flights, car pickup and return times, hotel sequence, room details, window-seat requests, parking costs, breakfast timing, dinner backups, receipt needs, and cancellation dates.
events.scenario_brief: The Pacific Northwest loop is ready to book. The chosen plan is open-jaw: Sunday afternoon Salt Lake City to Portland and Friday midafternoon Seattle to Salt Lake City, with one one-way rental car from Portland airport to SeaTac. Three hotel holds expire tonight: a Beaverton breakfast-included queen room for Sunday and Monday, an Albany room for the late Tuesday arrival after the fair, and a Tukwila or SeaTac room for Wednesday and Thursday with parking clarity and walkable dinner options. Tessa needs to confirm the booking order before the rates roll.

events.continuity_hook: Handles the final Pacific Northwest timing changes after the main reservations are in place.
events.interaction_goal: Set the day-by-day departure timeline, confirm checkout and luggage handling, choose breakfast backups, adjust dinner and drive plans, and protect the Friday airport buffer.
events.scenario_brief: Ten days before departure, the first Portland school asks visitors to arrive at 7:15 a.m., the Beaverton fair adds a counselor dinner before the floor opens, and the Seattle return flight is moved 25 minutes earlier. Her flights, rental car, and hotels are already booked. The tighter points are Monday hotel departure, Tuesday dinner timing before the late drive to Albany, whether Albany breakfast opens early enough for the Eugene check-in, and how much buffer to leave for fuel, car return, and bag drop at SeaTac.
